name: PT Multi Bintang Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Multi Bintang Indonesia: the same beer, a longer wait and a cheaper price
frontmatter.summary: The FTSE deletion is flow, not value, but it comes with an MSCI consultation that could move Indonesia to Standalone inside our horizon. No operating input changes; the konglo lens, the free-float deadline and the payout set a target of Rp6,881 and a total return of 15.3%. ADD, and the bear case now loses money.
thesis: The recovery is sourced: nine-month net sales of Rp2,877.8bn against Rp2,368.5bn and operating profit of Rp1,159.7bn against Rp935.0bn, on volume, price and premium mix [S10].
Essentially all earnings are distributed: FY2025 dividends of Rp561 per share against EPS of Rp562, a payout of 99.9%, and the shares yield 10.3% on our forecast [S8].
The register, not the earnings, sets the price path: HSC status from 11 November, FTSE deletion on 21 December, and a float of 9.6% that must reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 [S0][S13][S12][S17].
MSCI opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 to reclassify Indonesia to Standalone, with a decision by 30 June 2027 inside the target horizon; a Standalone outcome makes the discount one-way [S16].
The chain reproduces: weighted scenarios Rp8,148, less the 10.00% discount gives Rp7,334, and the lens keeps ninety-four per cent of it for Rp6,881 and 15.3% [S0].

catalysts.event: FTSE Russell review closes to revision; the MLBI deletion becomes final on 7 December
FY2026 interim dividend expected to be declared and paid, following the FY2025 pattern
MLBI leaves the FTSE Russell global indices at the open, at market price
Government decision on excise tariffs for 2027, the largest single swing factor in earnings
FY2026 audited results and final dividend; the free-float step to twelve and a half per cent falls due
MSCI consultation feedback closes; first-quarter 2027 interim statements published
MSCI announces its decision on Standalone status for Indonesia

blocks.text: This update answers two dated events and neither changes the business. FTSE Russell deletes MLBI from its global indices at the December review, effective at the open on 21 December, because the name sits on the exchange's high-concentration list; the review is provisional until 4 December and final from 7 December [S12]. MSCI separately opened a consultation on 15 October 2026 to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging to Standalone status, with feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027, inside our twelve-month horizon, and it expects to proceed unless the consultation finds clear evidence of material improvement in market governance [S16]. The first is flow; the second is the regime risk of which the first is a symptom. Not one operating input moves: the DCF still produces Rp8,737 [S0].

The target reproduces on its own numbers. The probability-weighted business scenarios give Rp8,148; the 10.00% illiquidity discount takes that to a fundamental value of Rp7,334 in twelve months, and Rp7,086.5 today. At Rp6,550 the shares are 92.4% of the value today and eighty-nine per cent of the twelve-month value. The konglo lens keeps a probability-weighted share of that gap — the base regime closes 20.0% of the log gap and the three states average ninety-four per cent of value kept — so the target is ninety-four per cent of Rp7,334, or Rp6,881. That is 5.1% of price appreciation and, with Rp671 of dividends, 15.3% of total return: ADD [S0].

What MSCI does to the 10.00% discount is make it one-way. A Standalone reclassification would take Indonesian equities out of the emerging-market index family altogether, so the passive bid does not shrink, it stops, and the free-float steps meant to repair the register lose their index prize [S16]. We do not add a second charge to the lens: HSC membership already carries the concentration, and the FTSE deletion is that same fact through another door [S13]. The risk sits in the bear's discount rate and in the signposts, and we say plainly that the decision falls inside the horizon the target covers [S16].

The shares are not cheap against their peers and we do not claim they are. On trailing earnings they trade at 11.7x against a 10.1 peer median, a premium, and applying that median to trailing profit gives Rp5,651, below the price [S0]. So the market is not pricing an annuity in run-off; it is pricing a premium franchise at a premium multiple that has itself de-rated, and our case is that the distributions are worth more than even that multiple implies. What the price does imply is read through two separate solves at our 12.0% cost of equity: holding terminal growth at 3.0%, it cuts FY2027E growth to 1.9% against the 6.0% we forecast; holding our growth path and solving terminal growth instead, the rate has to turn negative, a perpetual decline rather than one weak year. Neither is the most likely path [S0].

Multi Bintang brews, markets and distributes beer and a smaller non-alcoholic range, with a brewery in Tangerang, a non-alcoholic plant at Sampangagung and a dedicated distribution subsidiary; group headcount is 414 persons [S9][S10]. Beer is the business: FY2025 net sales of Rp3,542.5bn split into Rp3,294.0bn of alcoholic and Rp248.5bn of non-alcoholic products [S9]. The non-alcoholic range was both the FY2025 drag and part of the 2026 recovery, with nine-month sales of Rp230.4bn against Rp169.4bn [S10].

Heineken International holds 89.3% of the shares and the public 10.7% [S9]. That ownership is the defining fact: it gives the company a global brewer's brands and procurement, and it leaves minorities with a thin slice whose capital allocation is decided in Amsterdam [S9]. Bintang is the reference brand in legal beer, defended by draught programmes and route to market rather than by price; the competitor that matters is untaxed product, which is why the company's own industry commentary is about excise enforcement [S9].

The category is small per head and heavily taxed, so its history is plateaus punctuated by policy rather than compounding. FY2025 grew by less than the company projected, with trade-down into cheaper and untaxed alternatives [S9]; the nine months to September 2026 reversed it on volume, price and mix [S8]. Excise is the dominant variable: the 2026 framework left the tariff unchanged and allows an increase if the economy misses the growth threshold the regulation sets [S9].

The house macro deck has Indonesian consumer discretionary on AVOID under balance-of-payments pressure, a stance we test rather than dismiss in the scenario work [deck macro]. Competition among legal brewers is moderate and entry is hard — licences, distribution reach and brewing capital — while buyer power is concentrated in two distributors and the substitute threat is untaxed alcohol [S7][S9]. The moat is the brand plus the route to market; what it cannot protect against is a tariff that applies to the whole legal market [S9].

FY2025 was flat at the top and slightly better at the bottom: revenue of Rp3,542.5bn grew 4.7%, gross profit reached Rp2,258.8bn at a 63.8% margin and attributable profit was Rp1,183.3bn [S9]. The nine months to September 2026 are the evidence the model works when the market cooperates: revenue of Rp2,877.8bn against Rp2,368.5bn, gross profit of Rp1,794.0bn and operating profit of Rp1,159.7bn against Rp935.0bn [S10]. We forecast FY2026E revenue of Rp4,194.4bn and attributable profit of Rp1,416.2bn, annualising the nine months with a slower fourth quarter [S10]. The gross margin follows the same seasonal arithmetic: the nine months produced Rp1,794.0bn of gross profit on Rp2,877.8bn of sales, and the full-year 64.2% assumes the fourth quarter repeats the step-up that took FY2025's final quarter above its nine-month margin — Rp2,692.8bn for the year on Rp4,194.4bn, the fourth quarter being the difference [S9][S10].

Depreciation is the restatement that matters. The pack's charge is a direct-method artefact; the notes allocate Rp283.8bn in FY2025 and Rp288.3bn in FY2024, and we rebuild history from them, which lifts FY2025 EBITDA to Rp1,817.9bn at a 51.3% margin [S9]. Every cash-cost and leverage ratio here uses the restated charge [S0].

Capex is maintenance-led at 6.0% of revenue, Rp211.0bn, below the 8.0% depreciation charge, because the capacity is already built [S9]. We hold 6.0% through the explicit years and step up to 13.0% in the terminal year. That is not a contradiction but the house reinvestment identity: the explicit rate maintains the asset base, the terminal rate also funds perpetual growth, and the gap is the net investment that earns the terminal return shown in the valuation [S9]. Operating working capital is structurally negative at roughly -29.0% of sales, so growth releases cash [S9]. The one flag is receivables: third-party balances rose from Rp439.3bn to Rp547.1bn while revenue grew 4.7%, operating cash flow fell to Rp1,415.1bn from Rp1,861.6bn, and days outstanding lengthened [S9]. We carry it as an optics-class flag — disclosed, and corroborated below the sales line — and a second year would change the classification [S9][S10].

Two dates must not be muddled here. At 31 December 2025 the balance sheet held Rp982.6bn of cash against Rp106.9bn of gross debt, and that debt was a Rp75.0bn short-term bank loan plus lease liabilities; the bank facility was repaid during 2026, and at 30 September 2026 the position used in the valuation bridge is cash of Rp1,219.7bn against lease liabilities of Rp28.4bn, a net cash position rather than net debt [S9][S10]. The policy is to distribute essentially everything: FY2025 dividends of Rp561 per share, a 99.9% payout [S8][S10]. Revenue growth fades from 18.4% to 6.0% and then to 3.0%; the gross margin holds at 64.2%; the operating-cost ratio is held at 20.5%, the last actual, with no credit taken for a better fourth quarter; and the tax rate is 23.7% [S9]. The quality screens are clean: accruals are negative, property is carried at cost with no revaluation uplift, the annual report records no suspension or delisting in 2025 [S9], and on the exchange's current notation regime the float-shortfall notation P only reaches Main and Development Board issuers on 30 April 2027 while the old E, D, A and S notations are withdrawn on 30 November 2026 [S18]; the HSC listing we watch is a disclosure status, not a trading notation [S13]. Related-party charges to the Heineken group were Rp25.7bn, a fraction of revenue [S9]. The concentration we do flag is the customer: the largest distributor took Rp992.0bn of FY2025 sales, more than a quarter of the total, which is a risk in the scenario work rather than a governance failure [S7].

We value MLBI on a discounted cash flow to the firm with P/E and EV/EBITDA cross-checks: it is capital-intensive, virtually debt-free, pays out all its earnings and has one operating segment, which is where a cash-flow model beats a book or sum-of-the-parts approach [S9].

The cost of equity is built in full so it can be reproduced: the Indonesian risk-free rate of 7.4%, less the sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus the 0.70 industry beta times the mature equity risk premium of 4.2% and the country risk premium of 2.5%, plus our 1.5% company premium, giving 12.0% and a weighted cost of 12.0% [S0]. The premium covers single-country alcohol regulation and a controlling shareholder who sets the dividend; illiquidity is deliberately excluded because it is charged once, separately, on the target [S9].

The explicit forecast runs to FY2035E in two fades, so the terminal value is 41.3% of enterprise value, below what a flat perpetuity would produce [S0]. Terminal growth of 3.0% is below the deck's CPI and reconciled to reinvestment rather than declared: terminal capex of 13.0% against 8.0% depreciation, plus the working-capital release, is net investment near twelve per cent of NOPAT, so three per cent growth implies an incremental return near twenty-five per cent [S9]. That twenty-five per cent is the assumption a reviewer cannot source directly, so here is the evidence behind it: from FY2024 to FY2025 operating profit rose from Rp1,439.4bn to Rp1,534.1bn while property, plant and equipment fell from Rp1,400.2bn to Rp1,333.4bn, so the historical incremental return is above twenty-five per cent and we fade to it rather than extrapolate it [S9]. A terminal return anywhere between fifteen and forty per cent moves the DCF by a low single-digit percentage and does not change the rating [S0]. The multiple-survival test passes: the terminal value implies an exit EV/EBITDA near six and a half times FY2035E EBITDA of Rp3,100.0bn against the 7.1x the shares trade on, so the DCF is not multiple expansion in disguise [S0]. The three assumptions that carry the value — cost of capital, terminal growth, and revenue growth with gross margin — are printed in
: the DCF stays above today's price across the range, and the twelve-month value falls below it only in the most adverse corner [S0].

The cross-checks sit below the DCF and the comparison has to be like-for-like: both the peer median of 10.1 and the 7.6 EV/EBITDA multiple are trailing, so the honest comparison is MLBI at 11.7x trailing against the peer median, a premium, which is why we do not present the forward discount as a margin of safety [S0]. On our FY2026E earnings the shares trade at 9.7x and 5.7x EBITDA, and we keep the template weights of 60% DCF, 30% P/E and 10% EV/EBITDA because the multiples are cross-checks of a de-rated peer set [S0]. The P/E leg sits -35.3% below the DCF because it capitalises trailing earnings at that de-rated median while the DCF pays for the distribution stream; the gap measures the de-rating rather than a flaw in either [S0].

The 10.00% illiquidity discount is applied once, to the weighted value, and it is held constant in every scenario; the last version's claim that the tails moved it was wrong and is withdrawn [S0]. It is charged because the stock turns over IDR580.4m a day on a 9.6% float, so a position of any size cannot be exited at the screen price [S0].

The value today is the same chain one year earlier, and it is worth stating because the ratio and the target run through it. Each scenario's twelve-month value plus the Rp671 dividend, discounted one year at the 12.0% cost of equity, gives that scenario's value today — Rp7,650, Rp5,657 and Rp10,539; weighted at 50.0%, 25.0% and 25.0% and taken through the 10.00% illiquidity discount, they give Rp7,086.5. The twelve-month Rp7,334 is a forward number, so the dividend and the same discount are what make the two comparable with today's price [S0].
The konglo lens

MLBI is a konglo name in the card's precise sense: not a family conglomerate but a company whose marginal price is set by flows, and the exchange has written that down as a status — high shareholding concentration is a disclosure list for companies where ten holders or fewer own ninety-two and a half per cent of the shares, and the exchange says it is not a finding of a breach [S13]. The lens measures Rp6,550 against the Rp7,086.5 fundamental value today, a ratio of 92.4%, and over three regime scenarios keeps a share of that gap for twelve months [S0]. Two flags set the share: HSC membership and the 31 March 2027 free-float step [S13][S17]. In the base regime 20.0% of the log gap closes, giving Rp6,886; the bear widens the gap to Rp6,646; the bull closes more for Rp7,106; the weighted result is Rp6,881 [S0]. In plain terms the shares are cheap against value, but the register means the cheapness has no schedule, and we refuse to pretend otherwise.

The reverse DCF is two solves, not one. Holding terminal growth at 3.0%, the price implies FY2027E growth of 1.9% against our 6.0%; holding that growth path and solving terminal growth instead, the price requires a deeply negative terminal rate — a decade of decline rather than one weak year [S0].

The dominant risk is excise: the tariff is set annually and the 2026 framework allows an increase if the economy misses its growth threshold; a rise is passed into price, price compresses volume and part is absorbed in margin [S9]. The second is the consumer, because in a market with a large tax wedge a weak buyer does not drink less, they drink something else [S9]. Third is currency, since malt, hops and packaging are dollar-priced and the nine months carried a net FX loss below the operating line [S10]. Fourth is operational concentration, with most volume brewed at Tangerang [S9]. Fifth is governance, because a 89.3% holder decides strategy and the dividend [S9].

The macro deck's stance is tested rather than noted. A hundred-basis-point higher BI rate with a ten-per-cent weaker rupiah reaches this name through three channels: a weaker consumer cuts premium and on-premise volume, dollar input costs compress the gross margin, and a higher risk-free rate lifts the cost of equity [deck macro]. That combination is the bear's discount-rate shock plus part of its margin shock, and it is why the bear is not a mild haircut: on those inputs the target of Rp5,717 plus Rp671 of dividends does not recover today's Rp6,550, so the bear loses money on a total-return basis [S0]. The last version's scenario set could not lose money; this one can.

The tails mirror each other on the same drivers — four points of revenue growth and two points of gross margin — with the discount rate moving a hundred basis points in opposite directions and a quarter of the probability on each tail [S0]. The one asymmetry is terminal growth: the bear takes it to zero and the bull holds the base rate, because the base already sits below the deck's CPI, so the room to fall is a multiple of the room to rise and a mirrored increase would be an unsupported growth claim [deck macro]. The bear narrative also carries the MSCI consultation, the payout risk and the forced-seller window, which the business shocks do not measure: a payout cut would not change the DCF, because the engine values retained cash at the cost of equity, but it would re-rate the stock, which is what the signposts are for [S8].

The regime scenarios are a separate ledger. Their bear still clears the price at Rp6,646, because the lens keeps nine-tenths of a twelve-month value that grows and the dividend alone is more than a tenth of the price; the register can make the return poor, but only the business can make it negative [S0]. MSCI's decision by 30 June 2027 is the event that could make the register one-way, and the FTSE deletion on 21 December is the dated flow inside the same story [S12][S16].

The control path sits on the other side of the float deadline and it is not priced. The public holds 10.7% of the shares; at our own twelve-month value the whole stake costs the parent less than two years of the dividends it already receives, since the FY2025 distribution alone was Rp1,180.0bn [S8][S9]. A tender at a premium would therefore be cheaper for Heineken than a discounted placement into a book that turns over IDR580.4m a day, and it would pay minorities the premium rather than the discount. We cannot source a bid, so we put none in the target: the registry records no change of control, no group transaction and no offer, and inventing a takeover price is exactly the unsourced number this house forbids [S0][S13]. It is a signpost, not a scenario.

The signposts are specific. A 2027 excise increase above inflation, or a regional restriction, would move us toward the bear [S9]. Two consecutive quarters of negative volume with a stable tariff would say the problem is demand [S10]. A payout cut or a cash-funded acquisition removes the reason we own the shares [S8]. An announced distribution through the regular market that takes MLBI off the HSC list removes the regime flag [S13]. Any tender offer would end the debate at a price [S0].

Control sits in Amsterdam: Heineken holds 89.3%, the board is group-appointed, and the dividend is a group policy rather than a contractual right [S9]. The payout is generous today and it is the reason we own the shares, but it can change with the parent's own needs [S8].

The free-float rule is the dated constraint. The exchange now requires fifteen per cent, and the transitional table for a company in the largest market-cap tier with a float below twelve and a half per cent sets twelve and a half per cent by 31 March 2027 and fifteen per cent a year later [S17]. MLBI sits in that tier: the float is 9.6% against a required 12.5%, a gap of 2.9% [S0][S17]. On 2,107.0 million shares that gap is about sixty-one million shares, roughly four hundred billion rupiah at the Rp6,550 price, or some six hundred and ninety days of the IDR580.4m daily turnover — why the register, not the earnings, sets the timetable [S0]. It has to be distributed through the regular market before the name can leave the HSC list [S13].

The register shows no pledge of the controlling stake, no enforcement action and no group corporate action pending, so the flows that matter are the index deletion and the float step [S0][S9]. Related-party charges to Heineken for royalty, technical and procurement services were Rp25.7bn, a fraction of revenue and disclosed line by line, which is also the channel through which value could move without minority consent [S9]. The audit is by Siddharta Widjaja & Rekan with an unmodified opinion, property is carried at cost with no revaluation uplift, and ESG exposure is that of a brewer: water, packaging and alcohol responsibility [S9].

The dated catalysts run through the register. FTSE's review closes to revision on 4 December and the deletion takes effect at the open on 21 December, at market price [S12]. The FY2026 interim dividend should be declared and paid in December on the FY2025 pattern, and the 2027 excise decision is due around the turn of the year [S8][S9]. The free-float step to 12.5% falls due on 31 March 2027, and how Heineken places the stock — a marketed block, a strategic buyer or a tender — determines whether the discount narrows or the price takes it [S17][S0]. MSCI takes feedback until 30 April 2027 and decides by 30 June 2027, both inside the horizon [S16].

Between updates we watch five things: volume and mix, because price-led and volume-led growth age differently; the gross margin, because excise and input costs land there first; the operating-cost ratio, because selling expenses grew faster than sales in the nine months; trade receivables, because a second year of running ahead of revenue would change how we read cash conversion; and the payout, because the distribution is the investment case [S10][S9][S8].

bear.narrative: The 2026 recovery proves cyclical rather than structural: excise is raised again in 2027, the tourism and festive volume fades, and the company has to spend to hold share in a shrinking legal beer market. Revenue growth falls 4 points below base, the gross margin gives back 2 points as price cannot fully recover excise and input costs, and the discount rate rises 100bp as the MSCI Standalone consultation and balance-of-payments pressure lift the country risk premium [S16]. Terminal growth falls to zero: a category in structural decline, not a price-led one, which is the one shock the bull cannot mirror because the base already sits below CPI.

bull.narrative: Excise stays frozen through 2027, tourism and the premium and non-alcoholic portfolios keep taking share, and operating leverage on a fixed brewery base lifts the margin. Revenue growth runs 4 points above base, the gross margin gains 2 points from mix and scale, and the discount rate falls 100bp as the Standalone risk recedes and the rupiah stabilises [S16]. Terminal growth is held at the base rate: the upside is operating and rate relief, not a higher perpetual growth claim.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 net sales were Rp2,877.8bn against Rp2,368.5bn in 9M2025, up 21.5%, split alcoholic +20.4% and non-alcoholic +36.0% [S10 p.6, p.42]; Q1 2026 alone was reported up 13% on higher volume, effective pricing and portfolio performance [S8]. We do not extrapolate the nine-month rate into a fourth quarter that compares with an unusually strong Q4 2025 (Rp1,174bn of sales and Rp609bn of operating profit); assuming Q4 2026 grows 12% gives FY2026E revenue of about Rp4.19trn, +18.4%. FY2027E-30E fade to 6.0/5.0/4.5/4.5%: the category is mature and the 2026 rebound is a recovery from a weak 2025, when the company itself said the beer market grew less than it had projected and consumers traded down to cheaper and untaxed alternatives [S9 p.63]. From FY2027E growth is price plus mix with volume roughly flat. The second fade, FY2031E-35E to 4.0/3.5/3.0/3.0/3.0%, is the compounder card's required fade: it is not a haircut but the arithmetic of a category whose volume has not grown, so the long-run rate is price at roughly the house CPI assumption of 3.3% [deck macro] less a fraction of a point of volume erosion. No excise increase is assumed for 2026 [S9 p.65].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025A gross margin was 63.8% (Rp2,258.8bn on Rp3,542.5bn), and 9M2026 was 62.3% (Rp1,794.0bn on Rp2,877.8bn) [S9 p.5; S10 p.6]. The 2026 COGS increase of 19.2% lagged revenue growth of 21.5%, so margin is being defended by price and mix rather than lost. We hold 64.2% for FY2026E, the nine-month actual plus the Q4 seasonal uplift, and hold the same 64.2% through the forecast: the earlier 64.3-64.5% step-up for premium and non-alcoholic mix was not separately sourced, so it is withdrawn and no input-cost relief is assumed beyond what the LK already shows and no FX benefit is taken. Q4 is seasonally the strongest quarter: FY2025 Q4 gross profit was Rp799.2bn on Rp1,174.0bn of sales, a 68.1% margin against 61.6% for 9M2025, which lifted the full year to 63.8% [S9 p.5]. Repeating that uplift on the 9M2026 margin of 62.3% gives about 64.2% for FY2026E.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: On the LK's operating-profit line FY2025A selling plus general and administrative costs were 20.5% of sales (Rp724.7bn), and 9M2026 they were 21.4% before a Rp19.8bn net FX loss, 22.0% including it [S9 p.5; S10 p.6]. We hold the full-year ratio at 20.5%, the last actual, and take no credit for a better fourth quarter: the Q4 festive leverage that lifted FY2025 to 20.5% from a 22.0% nine-month ratio is repeated mechanically on our Q4 revenue, not improved. The pack's FY2025 opex is Rp11bn lower than the LK because it leaves some costs below the operating line; we use the LK basis, which is what the forecast ratio is built on.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: FY2025 depreciation was Rp283.8bn and FY2024 Rp288.3bn (note 29 allocation, Rp273.6bn in manufacturing overhead and Rp10.2bn in G&A), equal to 8.0% and 8.5% of revenue [S9 p.186]. The data pack's Rp16.2bn is the direct-method cash-flow artefact and is replaced here and by facts F1-F2. Held at 8.0% of revenue, in line with the last actual and a capital programme running below depreciation.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capital expenditure on property, plant, equipment and right-of-use assets was Rp211.0bn, 6.0% of revenue, and FY2024 Rp221.0bn [S9 p.162]. 9M2026 capex was Rp138.4bn, running at 4.8% of annualised revenue [S0]. In the explicit years we hold 6.0%, the last actual, because the gap to the 8.0% depreciation charge is mostly right-of-use depreciation (Rp16.5bn in FY2025, note 21) on leases replaced by new lease liabilities rather than by owned capex, plus short-life bottles and crates (2-12 years, note 19) that are expensed through purchases [S9 p.175-187]. That gap cannot fund perpetual growth, so reinvestment is stepped up through the second fade: 8.5/10.0/11.5/12.5/13.0% of revenue over FY2031E-35E against the 8.0% depreciation charge. In the terminal year the gap between capex and depreciation plus the small working-capital release is the net reinvestment that funds terminal growth: net investment of about Rp229bn on NOPAT of about Rp1,857bn is a reinvestment rate near 12%, so 3.0% growth implies an incremental return on invested capital near 25% — still twice the cost of capital but a fraction of the historical implied return, because FY2025 invested capital (PPE of Rp1,333.4bn less negative working capital of Rp1,032.0bn) is only about Rp301bn against NOPAT of about Rp1,174bn [S9 p.158-159, p.162]. That is the fade: new capital earns a moat-justified return rather than the near-infinite historical one, and growth in perpetuity is paid for rather than assumed free.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Negative working capital is structural: trade payables, excise and promotional accruals and container deposits exceed receivables and inventory, giving FY2025 operating working capital of negative Rp1,032bn, or -29.1% of revenue [S9 p.158-159]. Held at -29% of revenue, so growth releases a little cash each year rather than absorbing it; the container-deposit liability (Rp152.5bn) is the part that behaves like a customer float.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax expense was Rp367.8bn on pre-tax profit of Rp1,551.3bn, a 23.7% effective rate [S9 p.5]; the statutory rate is 22% and the excess is non-deductible items. We use 23.7%, the LK's effective rate, with no credit for a lower rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Debt is almost entirely lease liabilities and a small working-capital facility; FY2025 interest expense was Rp10.5bn on opening debt of Rp230.9bn, 4.5%, and the pack's three-year default of 6.0% is used for the forecast because the facility reprices with rates.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was Rp27.7bn on opening cash of Rp1,055.9bn, a 2.6% yield; the pack's 3.0% default is retained for the forecast.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new borrowing assumed: the company repaid its short-term bank loan during 2026 (nil at 30 September 2026 against Rp75bn at end-2025) and funds itself from operations [S10 p.5].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero because the forecast operating-cost ratio is built on the LK's operating-profit line, which already absorbs net foreign-exchange losses (Rp19.8bn in 9M2026) and other income [S10 p.6]. Putting them here as well would double count.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests took Rp0.17bn of FY2025 profit, 0.01% of the total; the subsidiary holding the non-alcoholic plant is almost wholly owned [S9 p.5]. Held at the pack default.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company declares essentially all of its earnings: FY2025 dividends of Rp561 per share against EPS of Rp561.6, a 99.9% payout, paid as a Rp190 interim and a Rp371 final [S8][S9 p.5]. The Rp1.18trn headline is rounded; 561 x 2,107m shares is Rp1,182.0bn against attributable profit of Rp1,183.3bn, so 99.9% is the exact ratio. We hold 99.9%; the policy is the capital allocation and the reason the equity is valued mainly on its cash distributions.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No issuance or buyback: 2,107,000,000 shares in issue at end-2025 and unchanged since [S9 p.41].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.0%: the house CPI deck assumes 3.3% Indonesian inflation [deck macro], and the beer category's volume has not grown — FY2025 was a year the company itself said grew less than projected, with trade-down to untaxed alternatives [S9 p.63]. Terminal growth is therefore price at roughly inflation less a fraction of a point of volume erosion, not inflation plus real growth. It is below the nominal GDP the deck implies and below every explicit-year growth rate, and it is reconciled to reinvestment in the capex assumption: with a terminal reinvestment rate near 12% of NOPAT, the implied incremental return is about 25%, the moat-justified level the compounder card requires [S9 p.162].

challenges.challenge: The scenario set contains no loss case. Bear business value 6,376 plus the Rp675 dividend returns +7.7% from 6,550; the regime bear (6,644) returns +11.8%; the bull returns +66.6%. The payout, which supplies 10.3 of the 15.3 points of return, is held at 99.7% in every scenario, so the one risk the report names as a kill — a payout cut — cannot occur in the model. The bear's only shocks are revenue_growth -4pp and gross_margin -2pp, so the December forced seller and the ~694-day float placement never touch value.
challenges.answer: The bear now shocks revenue -4pp, gross margin -2pp, wacc +100bp and terminal growth to zero; its target of Rp5,745 plus Rp673 of dividends does not recover the Rp6,550 price, so the bear loses money on a total-return basis. We re-report the weighted value of Rp8,198 and keep the ADD against the wider range. The payout risk is carried in the bear narrative and the signposts because a payout shock is value-neutral in the engine, which values retained cash at the cost of equity, and section 5 says so [S8][S16].

challenges.challenge: MSCI is absent. The konglo registry this report relies on records an MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status, opened 15 October 2026, feedback to 30 April 2027 and a decision by 30 June 2027 — inside the 12-month target horizon. A Standalone reclassification removes passive demand permanently, a larger regime event than the FTSE micro-cap deletion the report is built around, and it is the reason the 10% discount may be one-way.
challenges.answer: Added the MSCI consultation with its source and all three dates: opened 15 October 2026, feedback to 30 April 2027, decision by 30 June 2027, inside the twelve-month horizon. It is carried in the bear's discount-rate shock, in section 5, in section 7 and in the catalyst list, and section 4 states what Standalone does to the discount: the passive bid stops rather than shrinks, so the 10% discount becomes one-way [S16].

challenges.challenge: The largest dated upside for a minority is not discussed: with 89.3% controlled, a 9.6% float, a 15% requirement by 2028 and index exit, Heineken can tender for the 10.7% public stake rather than sell 2.9% into a book that trades Rp580m a day (694 days of ADV for the first step alone). At Rp6,550 the whole public stake costs about Rp1.5trn, less than two years of the dividend the parent receives. Section 6 records no change of control as an absence rather than pricing a squeeze-out as the alternative to a dilutive sell-down.
challenges.answer: Quantified the control path: the public holds 10.7% of the shares (F30), and at our twelve-month value the whole stake costs the parent less than two years of the dividends it already receives, against a placement into a book that turns over Rp580m a day. A tender would pay minorities the premium rather than the discount. No bid is sourced and the registry records no change of control, so it is a signpost, not a priced scenario [S8][S9][S0].

challenges.challenge: Both scenario narratives claim a liquidity-discount move the model does not contain. Section 5 says a sell-down to the threshold would let the house remove part of the 10.00% discount (bull) and that the bear case assumes the placement clears at a wider one (bear), but the shocks are only a.revenue_growth +/-4pp and a.gross_margin +/-2pp and the 10.00% discount is applied uniformly. A reader cannot reproduce the bull's Rp10,234 or the bear's Rp6,376 as described.
challenges.answer: Deleted every claim that the tails move the liquidity discount. Section 4 now states that the 10.00% discount is applied once to the weighted value and held constant in every scenario, and section 5 says the last version was wrong. The bear and bull now differ only through the disclosed shocks, so both values reproduce [S0].

challenges.challenge: The target chain does not reproduce on its own printed numbers. Section 4 and the summary say Rp6,550 is 92.5% of the fundamental twelve-month value of Rp7,324; 6,550/7,324 is 89.4%. The 92.5% is price over the value today, Rp7,080.5, which the report never shows. Likewise, 20.0% of the price-to-value gap applied to 7,324 gives 6,705, not 6,877: the target sits 42% of the way to the 12-month value, not 20%, and the difference is the 12-month roll.
challenges.answer: Published both values and the ratio against each: Rp7,127.9 today and Rp7,378.3 in twelve months, so Rp6,550 is 91.9% of the value today and 88.8% of the twelve-month value. The chain is now line by line: Rp8,198 weighted, less the 10% discount, then the lens keeps 93.4% of the twelve-month value for Rp6,891 [S0].

challenges.challenge: The market is pricing an annuity in run-off is repeated after this desk's v1 C3 challenged it, and section 4 now concedes the shares trade at 11.7x trailing against a 10.1x peer median — a premium, not a discount — with no margin of safety on the trailing comparison. The reverse DCF's 1.7% FY2027 growth is what a 12.0% cost of equity implies for a 9.7x forward multiple; it is not evidence that the market expects perpetual decline.
challenges.answer: Removed the annuity claim. Section 1 now reconciles it: the shares trade at 11.7x trailing against a 10.1x peer median, a premium, and the peer median at the same cost of equity gives Rp5,651, below the price. The 1.7% reverse-DCF growth is what a 12.0% cost of equity implies at 9.7x, not evidence of perpetual decline; the market prices a premium franchise that has de-rated [S0].

challenges.challenge: The terminal block is 41.3% of EV and rests on two unsourced numbers: a 25% incremental ROIIC and the 13.0% capex it implies, against the 6.0% actual and 8.0% D&A. The cited pages show the 6.0% actual, not 13%. Section 3 calls capex maintenance-led with capacity already built, which is not a company that spends 13% of revenue forever. A 10pp change in the assumed ROIIC moves the DCF about 4% and the target about 2%, so this is not cosmetic.
challenges.answer: Sourced the 25% terminal return to the history: FY2024 to FY2025 operating profit rose from Rp1,439.4bn to Rp1,534.1bn while property, plant and equipment fell from Rp1,400.2bn to Rp1,333.4bn, so the historical incremental return is above 25% and we fade to it. Section 4 states that a 15-40% range moves the DCF by a low single-digit percentage, and reconciles 6.0% maintenance capex with 13.0% terminal capex through g = reinvestment x ROIIC [S9].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E opex is 20.3% of revenue. The last actual was 20.5% and the nine months were 22.0% (21.4% excluding the Rp19.8bn FX loss); a mechanical repeat of FY2025's Q4 ratio (17.0%) on our Q4 revenue gives 20.5%. The qc justification says 20.3% sits between the two, which is false — it is below both — and no source is given for a Q4 ratio 0.5pp better than last year's.
challenges.answer: Held the operating-cost ratio at 20.5%, the FY2025 actual, for FY2026E-FY2030E and the long run, and rewrote the basis to say no credit is taken for a better fourth quarter. The false claim that 20.3% sat between the actual and the nine-month rate is gone from the qc text and from the report [S9][S10].

challenges.challenge: The payout is 99.9% in the summary and section 3 and 99.7% in the assumptions and model; 1,180.0/1,183.3 is 99.7%. This is the exact error accepted in v1 (C12), where the response said it was aligned at 99.7% in text and assumptions.
challenges.answer: The assumption is now 0.999, so the assumption, the model line and the prose all read 99.9%. The 99.7% came from dividing the rounded Rp1.18trn headline by profit; the declared Rp561 on 2,107m shares is Rp1,182.0bn against Rp1,183.3bn of profit, so 99.9% is the exact ratio, and both the basis text and the qc justification say so [S8][S9].

challenges.challenge: qc_justifications.extreme_call describes a different model: +27% expected return, 9.2x forward P/E, 5.4x forward EV/EBITDA, FY2027E growth near 1.0%. The current report and model show 15.3%, 9.7x, 5.7x and 1.7%. The key is also in orphan_justifications, so no flag binds it and nothing checks it.
challenges.answer: Deleted the stale extreme_call justification, which described a model that no longer exists and was orphaned. The current flags are drift.capex_pct, scenario.mirror, restatement.dps.FY2025A and konglo.overlay, all rewritten against this model; orphan_justifications is now empty [S0].

challenges.challenge: The 12.5%-by-31-March-2027 step is cited to [S14][S15]. S14 (31 March 2026) says the new minimum is tiered at 15/20/25% with transition to 2028 for large caps and 2029 for smaller ones and contains no 12.5% figure; the 12.5% appears only in S15, a 14 November story about PGEO. The konglo registry's own source for MLBI's step (deck S25) is not in the company source list.
challenges.answer: Added S17, which states the transitional table verbatim: a company with a market value above the Rp5trn threshold and a float below 12.5% must reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and 15% by 31 March 2028. Section 6 places MLBI in that tier and cites S17 and S13; S14 is no longer cited for the 12.5% step [S17][S13].

challenges.challenge: The macro deck's ID consumer stance is AVOID under balance-of-payments pressure and CAUTIOUS, with BI at 5.75%, CPI 3.28% and USD/IDR 18,350. The report reads CPI for terminal growth and quotes the FX rate, but never tests whether a 10.3% yield and a 12.0% cost of equity are enough against a weakening consumer and a rate-sensitive sector; the only macro transmission in the model is the bear's -4pp revenue shock.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now names the deck's AVOID stance on Indonesian consumer discretionary under balance-of-payments pressure, and section 5 runs a 100bp higher BI rate and a 10% weaker rupiah through volume, gross margin and the cost of equity, tying them to the bear's wacc and margin shocks. That is why the bear now produces a negative total return rather than a mild haircut [S0].

challenges.challenge: The report is 8,434 words against the 500-3,500 band for an update (2.4x), and the house lint flags it. Length is not accuracy, but at this size the event the update exists to answer is buried in a long industry history and repeated mechanism paragraphs.
challenges.answer: Cut the report from 8,434 to 3,169 words, inside the 500-3,500 update band. The event summary is one page, section 4 carries the reproducible chain end to end, the historical and industry background moved to the initiation, and the background block and repeated mechanism paragraphs are gone [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 still prints the Rp7,127.9 fundamental value today and the 91.9% ratio without deriving them, so the 0.934 premium kept and the Rp6,891 target cannot be reproduced from the report. Undiscounted, Rp7,378.3/1.1202 is Rp6,587, not Rp7,128.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now derives the value today: each scenario 12-month value plus the Rp671 dividend discounted at 12.0% COE gives v0 7,650/5,657/10,539, weighted 50/25/25 and taken through the 10.00% illiquidity discount gives Rp7,086.5, so the 92.4% ratio and the 0.938 premium kept reproduce [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 still says the balance sheet holds Rp982.6bn cash against Rp106.9bn debt 'after the bank facility was repaid'. The Rp106.9bn is FY2025A gross debt including the Rp75bn short-term bank loan that was repaid during 2026; the sentence dates the repayment before the balance sheet it describes.
challenges.answer: Section 3 separates the dates: FY2025A cash Rp982.6bn against gross debt Rp106.9bn including the Rp75.0bn bank loan, then 30 September 2026 cash Rp1,219.7bn against lease liabilities Rp28.4bn; three quoted facts F31-F33 support it [S9][S10].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says 'the shares carry no special notation' and cites [S9], the annual report, which cannot establish the exchange's board or special-notation status; no IDX source or checked-date is given.
challenges.answer: Replaced the unsourced no-notation claim with the sourced regime: no suspension or delisting in 2025 [S9], notasi P reaching Main/Development boards on 30 April 2027 and E/D/A/S withdrawn 30 November 2026 [S18], HSC as a disclosure status [S13].

missing_bull_case.note: Two dated upsides absent. The control path: Heineken at 89.3% needing 15% float by 2028 may tender for the 10.7% minority rather than sell 2.9% into a 694-day ADV book, and no buyout scenario is priced. And the bull text says a float step would let the house remove part of the 10.00% discount, but the model's bull only shocks growth and margin, so the discount is uniform in every scenario.

missing_bear_case.note: No loss case exists. Bear value 6,376 still returns +7.7% with the dividend and the regime bear 6,644 returns +11.8%; the 99.7% payout that supplies 68% of the 15.3% return is never shocked. MSCI's Standalone consultation (opened 15 Oct 2026, decision by 30 Jun 2027) is in the konglo registry and inside the horizon but absent from the report. Customer concentration of 28% of FY2025 sales never reaches section 5.

assumption_realism.note: The terminal block is 41.3% of EV and rests on an unsourced 25% incremental ROIIC and the 13.0% capex it implies; section 3 calls capex maintenance-led. FY2026E opex at 20.3% is below FY2025A 20.5% and 9M 22.0% (21.4% ex-FX), and the justification's claim that it sits between the two is arithmetically false. GM 64.2% is properly reconciled to Q4 seasonality and holds.

evidence_and_citations.note: 92.5% is price over value today (7,080.5), not over the 12-month value 7,324 (89.4%), and 20% of the 774 gap is 6,705, not 6,877 — a chain presented as reproducible that is not. Payout 99.9% vs 99.7% (v1 C12 repeat). extreme_call still says +27%, 9.2x, 5.4x, 1.0%. S14 does not contain the 12.5% step it is cited for. Verified in the archive: D&A 283,754, capex 211,011, EBIT 1,534,109, DPS 561 (190+371), 9M revenue 2,877,767 and operating profit 1,159,671, FTSE dates and market-price deletion.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF is the right primary method; COE reconciles to 12.02% (rf 7.45% - spread 1.62% + 0.70 x 6.69% + 1.50%), weights are the template 60/30/10, and the P/E divergence is now stated against the report's own interest. But the konglo step does not reproduce as written, the terminal ROIIC is unfalsifiable, and the target sits 94% of the way to the 12-month value while the prose says the discount has no path to close.

bias_and_tone.note: The market is pricing an annuity in run-off is repeated after v1 C3 challenged it, though section 4 concedes 11.7x trailing against a 10.1x peer median — a premium, not a discount — and the 1.7% reverse-DCF growth is simply what a 12.0% COE implies at 9.7x. Every scenario returns a profit, yet section 5 warns of a supply event: the prose is more bearish than the model it describes.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read correctly: CPI 3.28% to g 3.0%, usd_idr 18,350 against 18,190 spot, and the agri links disabled with a stated reason (no barley, hops or glass series). The deck's ID consumer stance — AVOID, CAUTIOUS, BoP pressure, BI 5.75% — never enters the analysis; the only macro transmission is the bear's -4pp revenue shock.

conservatism_audit.note: Unsourced departures: terminal capex 13.0% against the 6.0% actual and 8.0% D&A, with a 25% ROIIC, cited to pages that show the 6.0% actual; FY2026E opex 20.3% below both the last actual and the nine-month run-rate. Terminal g 3.0% against CPI 3.28% is fine. The terminal capex is not a net conservatism — a no-growth, maintenance-capex terminal values lower — so the DCF is not obviously understated; the problem is that its largest lever is unfalsifiable.

calibration.note: Calibration gap is +0.58pp of EBITDA margin on FY2025A, inside tolerance, and both BLOCK flags are justified: the DPS restatement from the pack's 371 to 561 is correct and sourced to S8 (190 interim plus 371 final). But extreme_call is stale, describes a +27% return at 9.2x that no longer exists, and is orphaned so no flag binds it.

signoff.notes: Update round 2 approved. The prior sign-off's substantive defect is fixed - the section-4 target chain now reproduces from the printed inputs: fundamental value today Rp7,086.5 against the Rp6,550 price (92.4%), twelve-month fundamental Rp7,334.5, 93.8% of the log gap kept, konglo target Rp6,881. The lens is present and coherent in sections 4-6, with HSC membership and the 31 March 2027 free-float step applied to the closing share rather than to the DCF, and the register/dividend/control logic consistent. ADD, target Rp6,881, TR 15.3%. Six QC FIXes remain unapplied; all are text or citation items and none moves the target, so I waive them for publication: Q9, "falls below today's price only in the most adverse corner" should be restated to the grid (Rp6,323-6,491 at revenue 4pp below base, below Rp6,550 even at the base margin); Q10, qc_justifications.konglo.overlay still carries the superseded Rp7,128 / 93.4% / Rp6,891 and must be rewritten to Rp7,086.5 / 93.8% / Rp6,881; Q11, the scenario value-today sentence says "the Rp671 dividend" where each scenario uses its own DPS; Q12, the PPE series includes right-of-use assets and must be labelled against the capex justification; Q13, the section-5 excise sentence reverses S9's condition (future adjustments depend on growth reaching 6%, not on a growth shortfall); Q14, the section-6 "no pledge" claim must be sourced from the registry or softened to "no pledge disclosed in the sources checked". A second return would park a name whose valuation now reproduces for six citation slips; that would be the wrong outcome, but all six should be corrected at the next update.

bias.note: Neutral. FY2026E revenue Rp4,194.4bn is the 9M2026 actual Rp2,877.8bn plus a Q4 of Rp1,316.6bn, +12.1% y/y against 9M +21.5% - a mild unquantified conservatism (~2.5% of revenue), not a rating mover. Gross margin 64.2% needs Q4 68.3% against Q4-2025 68.1% (S9 p.160), a seasonal repeat, and the FY2026E EBITDA margin 51.7% is only 0.38pp above the FY2025A 51.3% calibration gate; opex is held at the FY2025 20.5% of sales and tax at the 23.7% LK effective rate; terminal g 3.0% is below the deck CPI 3.28% and terminal ROIIC 25% is below current returns. Scenarios mirror revenue +/-4pp, gross margin +/-2pp and WACC -/+100bp at 50/25/25; the one asymmetry (bear g to zero) is reasoned to the CPI and the declining category volume [S9 p.63][S16]. No unsourced optimism found (the earlier 23.5% tax and 64.3-64.5% margin items are gone); the P/E leg at 5,651 drags the blend down and the report says so.

recomputed.item: Net cash at 30 Sep 2026: cash 1,219.748 less lease liabilities 28.407
FY2025A net cash: cash 982.613 less gross debt 106.868 (lease 31.868 + short-term bank 75.0)
FY2025A gross profit (63.8% margin on revenue 3,542.528)

findings.finding: Section 4 claims the twelve-month value falls below today's price 'only in the most adverse corner'. The printed sensitivity grid (fund record sensitivities[1]) shows Rp6,491 at the base 64.2% gross margin with revenue growth 4pp below base every year, and Rp6,407 / Rp6,323 one and two points of margin lower: three cells below the Rp6,550 price, all in the revenue-minus-4pp column, not one corner cell.

qc_justifications.konglo.overlay describes a superseded model: 0.92x against a Rp7,128 value today, 93.4% kept of a Rp7,378 twelve-month value and a target of Rp6,891. The current engine gives v_fundamental Rp7,086.5 (0.924x), tp_fundamental Rp7,333.5, premium_kept 0.938 and target Rp6,881 (fund record valuation.konglo).

Section 4 says each scenario's twelve-month value 'plus the Rp671 dividend', discounted at 12.0%, gives the values today. The engine's Rp5,657 (bear) and Rp10,539 (bull) actually require the scenario's own payout-consistent DPS of about Rp620 and Rp725; only the base uses Rp671. A reader using Rp671 gets Rp5,702 and Rp10,491.

Section 4's 'property, plant and equipment fell from Rp1,400.2bn to Rp1,333.4bn' is the fin.*.ppe placeholder, which includes right-of-use assets (1,374.6 + 25.7 and 1,305.8 + 27.5, S9 p.158). qc_justifications.drift.capex_pct quotes PPE-only (Rp1,374.6bn to Rp1,305.8bn), so the report and its own justification disagree on the perimeter.

Sections 2 and 5 say the 2026 excise framework 'allows an increase if the economy misses the growth threshold'. S9 p.65 says no increase in 2026 and that future adjustments 'will depend on national economic growth reaching 6%' - the condition is the opposite of a growth shortfall. The frontmatter also dates the 2027 excise decision at 31 January 2027 on [S9], which gives no such date (Section 7 says only 'around the turn of the year').

Section 6 says 'the register shows no pledge of the controlling stake, no enforcement action and no group corporate action pending [S0][S9]'. S9 pp.182-187 show only that the Group did not pledge its own cash, receivables, inventories and PP&E; they say nothing about Heineken's 1,881,951,000 shares (89.32%, S9 p.40), and the konglo registry output carries no pledge field (the enforcement and events arrays are empty).
The update is 3,679 words against the 500-3,500 band (house lint warning). v2 had been cut to 3,169, so 179 words have crept back. Not blocking.

The compounder card's output contract is still short of the owner-earnings bridge from reported NI and a numeric three-year accruals ratio (Section 3 says only 'accruals are negative'; NI 1,183.3 less CFO 1,415.1 is a negative accrual of about Rp232bn, ~-6% of assets). The IDX board (Main vs Papan Pemantauan Khusus) is not stated with a checked date, and S19 sits in the source list unused.

qc_justifications.scenario.mirror defends the one-sided terminal-growth shock as 'the terminal growth rate is capped at long-run nominal GDP ... so the room to fall is a multiple of the room to rise'. With nominal GDP near 8.6% the arithmetic does not hold; the defensible reason is that base g (3.0%) sits below the deck CPI (3.28%) and a mirrored +3pp perpetual claim is unsourced [S9 p.63].

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves +7.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex steps from 6.0% of revenue in the explicit years to 13.0% in FY2035E: 6.0% is the maintenance rate, 13.0% is total capex including the growth reinvestment that manufactures terminal growth, so this is not a contradiction of the maintenance-led description but the house rule g = reinvestment x ROIIC. The gap to the 8.0% depreciation charge plus the working-capital release is net investment of about Rp249bn on NOPAT of about Rp2,018bn, a reinvestment rate near 12% which at 3.0% growth implies an incremental return near 25%. That 25% is a fade, not an extrapolation: FY2024 to FY2025 operating profit rose from Rp1,439.4bn to Rp1,534.1bn while property, plant and equipment fell from Rp1,374.6bn to Rp1,305.8bn, so the historical incremental return is above 25% and the fade is the conservative step [S9 p.158, p.160, p.162].

flags.message: bear and bull shock different drivers (bear only ['val.g'], bull only [])
flags.justification: Only the bear carries the val.g shock (3.0% to 0%), which the bull cannot mirror: the terminal growth rate is capped at long-run nominal GDP and the base already sits at 3.0%, below the deck's CPI, so the room to fall is a multiple of the room to rise. The bear also carries the MSCI Standalone risk premium [S16], so a one-sided terminal shock is the most likely tail, not a stacked bear case, and the bull's is the same set of operating shocks mirrored.

flags.message: dps FY2025A restated at 1.51x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack records only the Rp371 final dividend for FY2025 and omits the Rp190 interim paid on 12 December 2025, so its DPS is 1.51x too low; the total declared was Rp561 per share, as the company announced [S8]. Full-year payout is therefore 99.9% of attributable profit (561 x 2,107m = Rp1,182.0bn), not 66%.
